executive_summary.company_overview: Thermify is a Welsh-headquartered climate tech SME at TRL 6–7 that installs modular mini data centres (HeatHub) in domestic properties, using waste heat from cloud computing workloads to replace gas boilers for residential heating and hot water. The company owns and remotely manages all hardware under a hardware-as-a-service model, simultaneously decarbonising residential heating and cloud infrastructure.
executive_summary.strongest_themes: Waste heat recovery from edge/distributed data centres is the single strongest funding theme — Horizon Europe CL4 2026–2027 explicitly names this technology. Secondary themes of residential decarbonisation, fuel poverty alleviation, and green cloud computing align well with UK and Welsh government priorities. The dual-sector nature (ICT + energy) is a genuine differentiator.
executive_summary.strongest_geographies: Wales is the strongest geography due to Thermify's HQ advantage unlocking Welsh Government programmes (Business Wales SMART, Ynni Cymru). The UK broadly is well-served by Innovate UK and UKRI programmes. EU/Horizon Europe is a high-value secondary geography given the near-exact CL4 call match.
executive_summary.key_constraints: The partner-led structure of major UK programmes (Ofgem SIF, Warm Homes SHF) means Thermify cannot lead applications and must find eligible lead partners. Horizon Europe requires a 3-country consortium. EIC Accelerator's sub-5% success rate is a significant resource risk. The programme-umbrella nature of Business Wales SMART means no confirmed open window.

strategic_recommendations.best_fit_strategy: Pursue Amazon Sustainability Accelerator immediately (open now, equity-free, directly relevant to Amazon's cloud interests). Simultaneously prepare a Horizon Europe CL4 consortium application as the highest-value long-term bet. Use Welsh Government programmes (Business Wales SMART, Ynni Cymru) as lower-risk near-term funding to bridge to larger rounds.
strategic_recommendations.best_geographies: Wales (home advantage, dedicated SME programmes) and EU/UK Horizon Europe (highest funding quantum and near-exact thematic match for CL4 waste heat recovery call).
strategic_recommendations.strongest_pathways: 1) Amazon Sustainability Accelerator — open now, direct, thematically aligned on green cloud; 2) Horizon Europe CL4 2026–2027 — near-exact call description, high value; 3) Business Wales SMART — Welsh SME R&D grant, recurring, low barrier; 4) EIC Accelerator — transformational funding if successful.
strategic_recommendations.key_partnerships: A Horizon Europe consortium requires 2+ EU partners from different countries — target a European university with data centre thermal management research (e.g. KTH Stockholm, TU Delft) and a European housing or energy operator. For Ofgem SIF and Warm Homes, identify a licensed DNO or registered social landlord willing to lead. A UK university partner (e.g. University of Wales) would unlock KTP funding.
strategic_recommendations.capability_gaps: Thermify needs to demonstrate measurable carbon savings per unit at scale (not just pilot) for most grant applications. A formal Life Cycle Assessment and independently verified energy performance data would strengthen all applications. EU consortium-building capability is currently absent and needs development.
strategic_recommendations.key_risks: 1) Horizon Europe CL4 is highly competitive and requires consortium assembly — lead time is 6–12 months minimum; 2) EIC Accelerator's <5% success rate makes it a resource-intensive long shot; 3) Business Wales SMART has no confirmed open window; 4) Partner-led programmes depend entirely on finding willing eligible lead organisations.

company_profile.name: Thermify
company_profile.value_proposition: Thermify replaces domestic gas boilers with modular mini data centres (HeatHub) installed in homes, using waste heat from cloud computing to provide residential heating and hot water while simultaneously delivering cloud services to business clients.
company_profile.technology: Patented heat transfer technology embedded in modular server rack units (HeatHub) installed in domestic properties (sheds, garages); waste heat from compute workloads is captured and transferred directly into home central heating systems, with Thermify retaining ownership and remote monitoring of hardware. Electricity for compute is paid by Thermify, with separate metering.
company_profile.primary_outcome: Elimination of gas boiler dependency in homes and near-zero waste heat from data centre operations, delivering decarbonisation of both residential heating and cloud infrastructure simultaneously.
secondary_benefits: Reduced energy bills for low-income and vulnerable households
Lower-cost, greener cloud computing for business clients
Distributed data centre model removes need for large centralised cooling infrastructure
Social housing and fuel poverty relief applications
company_profile.trl: TRL 6-7 — patented technology validated in controlled trials (e.g. installation at SPECIFIC IKC, University of Wales); active pilot deployments underway including the SHIELD project; scaling toward 2,000 units/year production with HeatHub V2 in development
company_profile.website_summary: Thermify is a UK-based climate tech company that installs modular mini data centres — called HeatHubs — inside domestic homes to replace gas boilers. The compute hardware runs encrypted cloud workloads for business clients, and the waste heat generated is captured and fed directly into the home's central heating and hot water system. This 'use energy twice' model simultaneously decarbonises residential heating and cloud infrastructure, with Thermify owning and remotely managing all hardware.
company_profile.external_findings: Thermify has completed early-stage trials including a two-week installation at SPECIFIC IKC (a Welsh research centre) and is running a pilot called the SHIELD project, with partnerships including Simcott Renewables. The company ran an EIS-eligible crowdfunding campaign on Seedrs/Republic that overfunded with over 255 investors, with proceeds earmarked to scale production to 2,000 HeatHub units per year and launch the next-generation HeatHub V2. Media coverage from Solar Power Portal, The Re-Engineer, and Elemental London confirms growing mainstream interest in the technology.
